title: GenotypeGVCFs peak RSS against interval length at 51 samples
allocation_regime: common_ceiling_comparison (32 GiB container, 26 GiB derived heap)
why_this_supersedes_the_earlier_ratio: The 16 GiB attempt's per-contig ratios averaged about 0.28 GiB/Mb, but its two longest readings were clipped by the ceiling under test and it never completed the longest contig. Every point below was measured under a ceiling no reading approached, so the fit rests on unclipped data.

fit.interpretation: The relationship is affine, not proportional. A positive intercept of about 3.2 GiB is per-task overhead that does not shrink with the interval, which is why the naive peak-over-length ratio falls from 0.337 to 0.268 GiB/Mb as intervals lengthen. A slope through the origin would therefore understate short intervals: at 20 Mb it predicts about 5.6 GiB against this fit's 7.6 GiB.

assumption_if_used_for_interval_sizing.statement: Within this cohort size and reference, a shorter interval's peak RSS is predicted by the same affine fit.
assumption_if_used_for_interval_sizing.status: ASSUMPTION, not measured: E0 contains no chromosome-scale interval below 27.7 Mb, so the fit is interpolated at 20 Mb rather than observed there.
assumption_if_used_for_interval_sizing.directly_testable_by: E2a, which runs 20 Mb windows over the same cohort under the same ceiling and will measure this point rather than assume it.

explicitly_not_claimed.sample_count_scaling: Nothing here measures how peak RSS varies with sample count. Both coefficients were fitted at exactly 51 samples, and neither is extrapolated to 327 samples.
explicitly_not_claimed.other_conditions: Valid for this reference, GATK version, ploidy and HaplotypeCaller condition only.
explicitly_not_claimed.wall_time: Wall times in this run were measured with three tasks running concurrently and are not comparable to a task measured alone.
